text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — hosted-api (us-east-1) queue growing rapidly. GPU pool 'hosted-gpu-us-east-1' at 100% alloc, queue length > 12k, p95 jumped from ~300ms to 3.2s, p99 ~72s. Autoscaler create errors observed. Investigating. https://redwood.ops/incidents/4487654321 :pager:

Alex (oncall): saw the bot. I'm on it. dumping autoscaler logs now. tagging @Priya for platform-level fallback routing.

Alex (oncall): logs show repeated create failures: `autoscaler: failed to provision instance: quotaExceeded` and `provisioner: rate limit exceeded (429)`. Looks like provisioner leader is reattempting and hitting cloud API rate limits.

Jamie (sre): can we open fallback to dedicated pool for critical tenants? We should also enable global token rate limit to avoid more queue growth.

Priya (platform): I can enable routing to dedicated pools for flagged customers. Giving me list of top 20 by qps? @Lina can you start triage with CS?

Lina (cs): pulling customer impact now. Initial pass: 7 premium customers show elevated 5xx (mostly 504/timeouts), ~18k unique requests failed in the last 10m. Noting Tier-A customers: OrbitLabs, QuickReply, TutorAI. I'll start notifying account reps.

Maya (infra): infra view — cloud provider returned `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` for instance creations in us-east-1a/b; autoscaler thrashing due to backoff loop. Provisioner leader had a brief restart at +4487654342 which correlates with spike.

Alex (oncall): temp mitigation plan: 1) enable route-fallback to `dedicated-emergency-1` for top 10 tenants, 2) enable conservative global rate limit for non-authenticated/anonymous traffic, 3) scale up edge-cached small-embedding tier to absorb -> runbook commands below.

Alex (oncall): running command to open fallback routing now:
```
rb route set-fallback --from hosted-api --to dedicated-emergency-1 --customers orbitlabs,quickreply,tutorai --reason "evening traffic wave"
```

DeployBot: deploy triggered: route-change v2026.03.15-evac1 -> canary -> 3 pods. Watch logs at https://deploys.redwood/route-change/evac1

Jamie (sre): enabling protective rate limits (soft) to 60r/s global for 15m:
```
rb limits set --scope global --rps 60 --duration 15m --note "emergency evening wave"
```

Maya (infra): I'm throttling non-critical batch jobs in the region to free up allocation and bumping low-priority eviction threshold. Running `infra quota bump low-priority 20%` now.

Alex (oncall): we still see inst create failures when autoscaler tries to bounce. Need to temporarily increase parallel creates and relax provider rate limits on our autoscaler (short term). Priya, do you have perms to patch?

Priya (platform): applying emergency patch to autoscaler config to increase `cloud_api_parallelism` from 4 -> 12 and `create_backoff_initial` from 30s -> 5s to spread retries. Pushing now — will monitor.

IncidentBot: Update: route-change canary succeeded. 3/3 canary pods healthy, traffic shifted for specified customers.

Alex (oncall): monitoring p95/p99 — initial drop for migrated customers. Overall queue still high though (9k). We'll need to drain backlog and prevent further ingress.

Lina (cs): customer-notes: OrbitLabs reported 504s at 19:12 ET, QuickReply seeing 30% error rate. Sending CS incident ping to affected accounts and requesting cutover to emergency endpoints where possible.

Jamie (sre): additional mitigation: flip inference fallback to lower-memory quantized model for anonymous/low-priority requests to reduce GPU footprint. This will slightly affect quality but drop token compute by ~2.5x.

Alex (oncall): executing fallback toggle:
```
rb model set-fallback --service hosted-api --selector "priority:low" --model rwd-qlora-med-q8 --duration 30m --note "emergency evening wave"
```

Maya (infra): new autoscaler config applied — we're seeing fewer 429s from cloud API and provisioning is starting to succeed slowly. New nodes showing up but with slow join times (~45-60s).

DeployBot: autoscaler-config patch deployed: autoscaler:v1.9.3-patch -> rolling.

Alex (oncall): running backlog drain script to prioritize oldest requests and reject obviously malformed/huge requests:
```
./scripts/drain_queue --policy oldest-first --max-accept 2000/s --reject-patterns "Content-Length>5MB|multipart/form-data"
```

Jamie (sre): observed immediate effect — accepted rate steady ~1.8k/s and queue trending down from 9k -> 3.6k in 10m. p95 dropping to ~600ms for routed customers. p99 still noisy ~8-12s for un-routed tenant traffic.

Lina (cs): putting status update in the customer-facing incident page. Notifying top 20 accounts we have mitigation in place and working on capacity normalization.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Jamie for overnight watch and follow-up postmortem. Key open items for handoff:
- Confirm autoscaler parallel create limits don't cause provider cost/abuse.
- Revert model fallback after stabilization (Priya to schedule).
- Postmortem owner and timeline (Maya + Jamie)
- CS customer comms follow-up (Lina)

Jamie (sre): taking it. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and then reduce rate-limits gradually if stable. Primary suspect: provider quota + leader restart caused autoscaler to oscillate and hit rate-limits, compounding evening traffic wave. Will collect traces and metrics for postmortem.

Maya (infra): creating short-term cloud quota request with provider and filing ticket: `CLD-REQ-9921`. Also adding provider-side rate-limit handling to autoscaler (follow-up).

Priya (platform): scheduling rollback plan for model fallback and route-change once queue < 1k for 15m.

Lina (cs): customer impact summary (prelim): ~25k total errors across region over 30m window, 7 premium customers affected with visible 504 spikes, estimated SLA exposure window ~00:17:00 (17 minutes peak). CS will send tailored notes.

IncidentBot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Current queue 3.2k. P95 overall 730ms, p99 9.1s. Handed to oncall: Jamie.

Jamie (sre): acknowledged. I'll open an incident follow-up doc and tag owners. Postmortem plan: root-cause hypothesis and remediation list by EOD tomorrow.

Alex (oncall): thanks team. If anything regresses, re-page same thread. :thumbsup:

---
Notes to postmortem (added inline):
- Root cause hypothesis: evening traffic wave exposed a window where autoscaler leader restart + cloud API throttles caused repeated create failures; autoscaler backoff/parallelism settings led to retry storms.
- Immediate mitigations that worked: route fallback to dedicated pools, protective global rate-limits, model fallback to quantized variant, throttle non-critical batch jobs, autoscaler parallelism bump, drain script.
- Action items: 1) Add exponential jitter + provider-rate limiter to autoscaler, 2) Run chaos test for leader restart with high qps, 3) Formalize emergency dedicated pool cold-start playbook, 4) Improve customer-facing status automation for reroutes.

End of thread.
